memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: That is why the well was called Beer Lahai Roi; it is still there, between Kadesh and Bered. - Gen 16:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A well in the desert gets a name: Beer Lahai Roi - "the well of the Living One who sees me." And Scripture adds a quiet detail: "it is still there." Long after Hagar's encounter, the well remained, a lasting marker of the day God met a broken woman in the wilderness. Others would pass by, draw water, and remember: this is the place where God saw someone.

There is something worth pausing on in this simple monument. Hagar's encounter with God was not a private, forgettable moment. It was marked, named, remembered - a permanent reminder in the landscape that the God who sees had shown up in that very spot.

We would do well to mark our own "wells." When God meets us in a wilderness - answers a desperate prayer, shows up in a dark season, makes His presence known when we felt most alone - it is good to remember it, to name it, to build a marker so we don't forget. Our memories are short, and we need reminders of God's faithfulness.

Throughout Scripture, God's people built altars and named places precisely so that later, in new troubles, they could look back and remember. "I will remember the deeds of the Lord" (Ps 77:11). What are your wells? Where has the God who sees met you before? Remember those places. They are meant to strengthen your faith for the wilderness you face now.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where are the "wells" in your life - places God met you before?
- How can remembering God's past faithfulness strengthen you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me remember the wells - the places You have met me in my wilderness. When new troubles come, let me look back and recall Your faithfulness, so that memory strengthens my faith today.
Amen.
